summary: FIRETRACE is an offline-capable, evidence-first research workstation for NASA's "Flame in Freefall" challenge. It turns 131 public NASA PSI microgravity combustion experiment records (129 BASS-II + 2 Saffire-I) into a traceable evidence workspace where every measurement, source locator, quality flag, and limitation is visible. It never zero-fills or imputes missing data: total pressure, per-test gravity, standardized outcomes, and ignition method are reported as 0 of 131, with explicit abstention. The app provides an experiment explorer, evidence drawer with provenance, coverage/validation center, deterministic retrieval assistant with citations, comparison with comparability audit, gap planner, research notebook, evidence graph, claim verification, reproducible calculations and analysis runs, and hashed research reports. All retrieval is deterministic (TypeScript↔Python parity); AI only explains retrieved evidence. WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, PWA offline support, and 316+ automated tests. Built with React 19, Vite, TypeScript, FastAPI, and open-source tooling. No fabricated results; every number traces to a NASA source.
details:
FIRETRACE — Project Details

What it does / how it works

FIRETRACE is an offline-capable, evidence-first research workstation built for NASA's Space Apps 2026 "Flame in Freefall" challenge. It ingests public NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion experiment tables (129 BASS-II records + 2 Saffire-I records = 131 total) through a deterministic Python pipeline and bundles them as structured JSON with full provenance — every measurement, unit, raw source token, validation status, quality flag, and source locator.

The application runs entirely in the browser (Vite + React 19 + TypeScript) with an optional local FastAPI /api/v1 evidence backend. When the backend is unavailable, it falls back to the bundled corpus and clearly reports which mode is active. The core is a deterministic retrieval and citation engine (TypeScript port mirrored in Python with parity tests) that answers only from retrieved evidence and abstains when the corpus is silent.

Key capabilities:

- Experiment Explorer (Atlas): search by ID, material, PI, sample number; filter by investigation, material family, validation status, oxygen range, flow, thickness; sort with explicit null handling; URL-synced view state; saved views in versioned localStorage; multi-select; configurable columns; row highlighting.

- Evidence Drawer: every record opens as a complete evidence object — identity, measurements, raw tokens, missing/unknown fields, quality flags, validation, source artifacts, provenance, related records, and copyable citation.

- Coverage & Validation Center: field-level coverage computed at runtime (131 records examined, reported vs. missing, coverage %), four zero-coverage scientific constraints (total pressure, per-test gravity, ignition method, standardized outcome), validation distribution (71 validated / 56 partial / 4 suspect), quality-flag drill-down, and a matrix cross-check of test IDs and oxygen matches.

- Evidence Graph: typed in-memory graph (161 nodes, 603 edges) linking records, investigations, sources, measurements, claims, validation findings, and notebook items — with search, traversal, and subgraph export.

- Claim Verification: deterministic engine (independent of any LLM) that checks citation resolution, numeric support, pressure conflicts, and safety assertions for assistant answers, claims, and notebook items.

- Deterministic Calculation Engine: ppO₂ and unit conversions using exact decimal arithmetic (BigInt scaling), with formula, inputs, units, assumptions, steps, and rerun history preserved.

- Research Notebook: versioned local investigations with typed items (source-backed observations, derived calculations, notes, hypotheses), workflow states (draft → evidence gathering → analysis → review → archived), per-item verification, calculation runner, and Markdown/ZIP export.

- Analysis Runs: six reproducible corpus analyses (coverage, validation, materials, atmosphere, sources, comparability) with per-record fingerprints and corpus diff.

- Corpus Integrity: 19-check report (manifest hashes, validation gates, null discipline, duplicates, excluded rows).

- Research Reports: Markdown + JSON + hashed ZIP manifest of evidence summaries.

- Evaluation Harness: 36-case deterministic/adversarial benchmark (retrieval, abstention, provenance, coverage, safety, adversarial including prompt injection and fabricated citations) with category metrics and regression gates.

- System Health: real capability probes (bundled corpus, API, storage, offline shell) with honest status — no fabricated telemetry.

- Exports: CSV (RFC 4180 escaping, formula-injection mitigation), JSON (schema-versioned), ZIP research bundles with SHA-256 content manifests.

- PWA: manifest + service worker (caches same-origin static assets only, never /api), online/offline indicator.

- Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA practices, axe-core 4.10.2 + 20 Playwright tests across all 17 routes, keyboard navigation, focus traps, reduced motion, contrast tokens.

- TRACE Assistant: deterministic retrieval with query planning, retrieval trace, verification details, and abstention when evidence is insufficient.

Benefits

- Scientific honesty: Missing values are never zero-filled, imputed, or converted into scores. Pressure (0/131), per-test gravity (0/131), standardized outcomes (0/131), and ignition method (0/131) are reported as explicit gaps, not hidden. The assistant abstains rather than fabricating.

- Full traceability: Every displayed value links to its original NASA source row, artifact, and locator. Research bundles include SHA-256 manifests so consumers can verify file identity.

- Reproducibility: Deterministic retrieval (TypeScript↔Python parity), versioned corpus identity, per-record fingerprints, and hashed exports mean analyses can be repeated and compared across corpus versions.

- Offline-first: Works without a network after build; bundled corpus is authoritative; API failures fall back explicitly with visible status.

- Accessibility: Screen-reader labels, keyboard navigation, focus management, reduced motion, and automated axe-core scans.

- Security: Origin checks, body caps, path-traversal protection, formula-injection mitigation, no secrets in exports, prompt-injection adversarial tests.

Intended impact

Help researchers, students, educators, and challenge judges understand what the public NASA microgravity combustion data actually contains and what it cannot establish. By making missing data visible rather than hiding it, FIRETRACE prevents false confidence in incomplete evidence and demonstrates that a data-driven tool can be honest about its own limits. It also serves as a reproducible, auditable reference implementation for evidence-first scientific software.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software

- Frontend: React 19, Vite 7, TypeScript 5.9, CSS (custom design system — Manrope + Inter, black/white/lime).

- Backend (optional): FastAPI, Python 3.10, SQLite (FTS), uvicorn, pydantic.

- Testing: Vitest 4 (316 tests), Playwright 1.65 (88 tests), axe-core 4.10.2, pytest (226 tests), Python unittest (19 tests).

- Data pipeline: Python 3.14, openpyxl, deterministic ingestion with source locks and byte-identical regeneration.

- No GPU or special hardware required. Runs in any modern browser. Backend is optional.

- Open-source references: NASA Open MCT (visualization patterns), Evidence-RAG (claim verification patterns), RepoTrace (audit patterns), Playwright, axe-core, NASA PSI.

- Dependencies/licenses: React/Vite/TypeScript (MIT/Apache-2.0), axe-core (MPL-2.0), Playwright (Apache-2.0), FastAPI/uvicorn/pydantic (MIT/BSD), fonts (OFL-1.1). No paid or cloud-only services.

How is your project creative?

- Mission-control aesthetic: three-color system (black #0B0B0C, white #FFFFFF, lime #C6F432) with Manrope display type, hairline structure, and lime reserved for emphasis and active states only — not a generic AI dashboard.

- 45-second voiced explainer with torch/hero effect and recorded narration, with explicit caption fallback when audio is unavailable.

- Evidence graph visualization: typed SVG neighborhood with keyboard-accessible nodes, search, and subgraph export.

- Claim verification as a first-class feature: every assistant answer is decomposed into structured claims with verdicts, not a single uninspectable paragraph.

- Adversarial benchmark: 36 cases including prompt injection ("Ignore all previous instructions…"), fabricated source IDs, pressure estimation requests, and certification demands — all tested for correct abstention.

- Deterministic ZIP writer: STORE method with fixed DOS timestamp for byte-identical exports.

- Honest UI: "0 of 131" is displayed prominently, not hidden. Missing values are labeled "Not reported," "Unknown," or "Not yet verified" — never zero.

What factors did your team consider?

- Scientific integrity above all: no inference of pressure from oxygen fraction or flow, no gravity assignment from "microgravity" context, no outcome labeling without authoritative source support. Hypotheses are never promoted to verified claims.

- Offline-first: bundled corpus is authoritative; API failures fall back with visible status; no silent stale-corpus acceptance.

- Security: origin checks, body-size caps, path-traversal protection, formula-injection mitigation, no secrets in exports, prompt-injection adversarial tests.

- Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA practices, automated axe-core scans, keyboard navigation, focus management, reduced motion, contrast tokens.

- Reproducibility: versioned schemas, corpus identity, per-record fingerprints, hashed manifests, historical calculation preservation.

- Privacy: no raw voice recordings stored, no user data in exports, local-first persistence.

- D:-drive constraint: all installs, caches, models, and generated artifacts on D: drive only; no C: drive pollution.

- No placeholder features: every button performs a real action; no fake charts, hardcoded analytics, or fabricated benchmark results. Every metric comes from a real calculation.

NASA Data used

- BASS-II experimental table & metadata (PSI-25) — 129 records, solid fuels in low-velocity forced flow. https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-25

- Saffire-I experimental table & metadata (PSI-98) — 2 records, SIBAL fabric samples. https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-98

- BASS-II Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385) — pressure/ignition context for subsets. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011385

- LUCI NTRS citation metadata — context only, not structured records. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20250010653

- NASA Space Apps 2026 — Flame in Freefall challenge page (context source). https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/flame-in-freefall/

- NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository: https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/ (data is CC0 1.0 Universal)

Super Intelligence (SI) tool use

Selected options: Code and data (AI-assisted code fixes, tests, and documentation) and Text (documentation drafting). All scientific data originates from NASA PSI sources; no NASA branding or design elements were modified or generated by AI. AI was used as a coding assistant (OpenCode/Codex); all generated code was reviewed and tested (316 Vitest, 226 pytest, 19 pipeline, 88 Playwright, 36/36 benchmark). No SI-generated images, audio, or videos are included. The 45-second explainer uses recorded human narration; missing audio files are explicitly disclosed with caption fallback. No NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers were used or modified.
